title: Federal calendar-day, 30-day and purchase quantity limits for scheduled listed chemical products
subtopic: Scheduled listed chemical product quantity limits
rule_summary: Under 21 CFR 1314.20(a) and 21 U.S.C. 830(d)(1), without regard to the number of transactions, a regulated seller (including a mobile retail vendor) may not in a single calendar day sell any purchaser more than 3.6 grams of ephedrine base, 3.6 grams of pseudoephedrine base, or 3.6 grams of phenylpropanolamine base in scheduled listed chemical products. Under 21 CFR 1314.20(b) and 21 U.S.C. 830(e)(1)(A)(ix)(II), a mobile retail vendor may not in any 30-day period sell an individual purchaser more than 7.5 grams of ephedrine base, 7.5 grams of pseudoephedrine base, or 7.5 grams of phenylpropanolamine base in scheduled listed chemical products. Under 21 CFR 1314.100, headed sales limits for mail-order sales, and 21 U.S.C. 830(d)(1) and (e)(2)(B), each regulated person who makes a sale at retail of a scheduled listed chemical product and is required under 21 CFR 1310.03(c) to submit a report of the sales transaction may not in a single calendar day sell to any purchaser more than 3.6 grams, and may not in any 30-day period sell to an individual purchaser more than 7.5 grams, of ephedrine base, pseudoephedrine base, or phenylpropanolamine base in scheduled listed chemical products. 21 CFR 1314.20 states no 30-day limit for a regulated seller that is not a mobile retail vendor. Separately, 21 U.S.C. 844(a) makes it unlawful for any person to knowingly or intentionally purchase at retail during a 30 day period more than 9 grams of ephedrine base, pseudoephedrine base, or phenylpropanolamine base in a scheduled listed chemical product, except that, of such 9 grams, not more than 7.5 grams may be imported by means of shipping through any private or commercial carrier or the Postal Service.
exam_relevance: Tests which party each figure binds and over what period: the 3.6-gram calendar-day limit binds every regulated seller whatever the number of transactions, the 7.5-gram 30-day limits bind mobile retail vendors and mail-order sellers, and the 9-gram 30-day figure is a statutory prohibition on the purchaser rather than a limit stated in 21 CFR 1314.20.

exceptions: Of the 9 grams a person may purchase at retail during a 30 day period, not more than 7.5 grams may be imported by means of shipping through any private or commercial carrier or the Postal Service.
common_confusions: The 9-gram figure does not appear in 21 CFR 1314.20; it is the 30 day purchase prohibition in 21 U.S.C. 844(a), which binds the person purchasing.
The calendar-day limit applies without regard to the number of transactions, so a second transaction on the same day counts toward it.
The limits are stated in grams of base, not in the weight of the product or a count of dosage units.
The 7.5-gram 30-day limits are stated for mobile retail vendors and for sellers whose retail sales must be reported under 21 CFR 1310.03(c), not for other regulated sellers.
